one_liner: Hands-on kennel job caring for U.S. Capitol Police working dogs: feeding, medicating, grooming, cleaning kennels, keeping medical records, and driving dogs to vets.
fit_summary: This role requires one year of specialized animal-care experience (canine feeding, grooming, health checks, sanitation, cage-washer use), and nothing on file shows Daniel has it. Daniel's strengths in policy, public engagement, and emergency-management consulting do not substitute, and the posting states there is no education substitution. Unless Daniel has undisclosed kennel, vet-tech, or shelter experience, this is not a realistic fit.
eligibility: Open to the public; U.S. citizenship required (no federal status needed).
One year of specialized experience equivalent to CP-03/GS-05 in canine care: sanitation, feeding, grooming, bathing, exercising, health checks, and transporting canines. No education substitution.
Must pass a full field background investigation and serve a one-year probationary period.
Must obtain and maintain a valid REAL ID U.S. driver's license and drive canines to appointments and between facilities.
Must be physically able to lift up to 75 pounds, restrain dogs, and work in adverse weather and kennel conditions.
keywords: liaison between handlers and veterinary personnel
strategy: Apply only if you have real, documentable animal-care work, paid or substantial volunteer, totaling at least one year full-time equivalent. List hours per week, because USAJOBS credits part-time and volunteer work proportionally.

If you do qualify, put the specialized experience first on your resume and keep it to two pages. Use the posting's exact terms, such as feeding, sanitation, health checks, medications, and transporting canines.
Frame your IEM experience only as supporting evidence: recordkeeping, coordination with stakeholders, and work in operational or emergency settings. Do not present it as qualifying experience.
Answer the assessment questionnaire honestly. Inflated 'expert' answers that your resume cannot back up can disqualify you or come out during the background check.
The posting asks for narrative KSA responses, so prepare short, specific examples for each animal-care KSA. Submit before the November 4, 2026 close.
Better use of your time: search U.S. Capitol Police, House, and Senate postings for community outreach, legislative affairs, or emergency-preparedness roles that match your policy and IEM background.
resume_bullets: Cared for [number] dogs at [kennel/shelter/clinic], including feeding, bathing, grooming, exercising, and daily health checks, [hours] hrs/week from [dates].
Cleaned and sanitized kennels, crates, and runs using [cage washer/power equipment/germicidal cleanser], following [facility] sanitation procedures.
At IEM, coordinated with [government clients/teams] on [emergency management task] and maintained [type of records], [hours] hrs/week, [dates].
interview_questions: Walk us through how you would perform a daily health check on a working canine and what signs would prompt you to call the vet.
Describe a time you handled or restrained a difficult or aggressive dog safely.
How do you keep accurate medical and feeding records when caring for multiple animals?
How would you handle being called in on a weekend or holiday to receive new canines or transport an injured dog?
watch_outs: Daniel likely cannot meet the mandatory specialized animal-care experience, and education cannot substitute for it.
The job is physically demanding: lifting up to 75 lb, risk of bites and scratches, and exposure to extreme weather and odors.
No telework, plus possible overtime on weekends and holidays, and a commute from Manassas to DC.
Promotion potential tops out at CP-04, so there is no built-in career ladder toward policy work.
